scope.description: Eligibility of support consumed for one public VerifyLeader future in a real leadership period, with fixed membership containing at least three voters and at least one nonvoter. Compare public completion with independently established eligibility of possible contributing peers.
assumptions: Non-Byzantine real target workers and correct in-memory transport/store behavior.
Unique validated member identities; no membership change, restart, user restore or leadership transfer during the checked interval.
The observer establishes absence of contributing remote voter replies for the selected future; inability to establish this is incomplete attribution, not a violation.
excluded: No assertion that VerifyLeader failure is necessary whenever current network reachability is low.
No requirement for eventual success, exact timing or a particular error.
No claim of stale application reads, divergent committed logs or crash durability.

parameters.success_condition: nil Error() on the correlated public future
parameters.forbidden_support: self plus only Nonvoter notifications when voter quorum is greater than one

units.rationale: Continue the accepted candidate with a conditional support-eligibility obligation. Source comparison identifies an authority API whose voter-derived threshold is fed by identity-free positive notifications from all replication peers. The tests cover voting-majority success and post-stepdown failure, leaving mixed-membership eligibility untested. This product derives a necessary support condition and preserves lease, negative-response and legitimate voter-support alternatives; it makes no execution claim.

audit_question.question: Can positive notifications from nonvoting replication peers satisfy a VerifyLeader future under fixed mixed membership without the voter support required for that public authority check?
audit_question.importance: VerifyLeader is documented as preventing stale local FSM reads after leadership loss. If nonvoter support can substitute for an authority-confirming voter quorum, public success may mislead a read caller. This question does not yet establish a stale application read or an incorrect log decision.
contexts: one VerifyLeader invocation through public completion
event_paths: bootstrap and actual election -> stable configuration -> VerifyLeader registration -> actual peer response production/delivery -> notifyAll -> vote -> leaderLoop future completion

supporting_behavior_ids.B-membership: Defines actual voter/nonvoter roles and replication eligibility.
supporting_behavior_ids.B-elect: Establishes a real leader before the check.
supporting_behavior_ids.B-authority-life: Lease expiry, higher-term stepdown and cleanup are protective competing events.
supporting_behavior_ids.B-commit: Shows separately voter-filtered log commitment; its guarantees cannot be assumed for VerifyLeader.
supporting_behavior_ids.B-verify-register: Establishes the pending-future registration and voter-derived threshold before principal positive notifications are consumed; it does not itself establish or consume F-peer-positive.
supporting_behavior_ids.B-verify-finish: Consumes the downstream F-verify-threshold and exposes public success or failure; this is a consequence of the principal notification consumption, not a direct F-peer-positive edge.

counterevidence: VerifyLeader returns errors on follower/candidate and on negative notification; leader exit fails pending verification.
Voter-only lease checks can end authority even if nonvoters respond.
Normal commitment explicitly excludes nonvoter matches; no incorrect log commitment follows from this registration asymmetry alone.
The API does not literally state a voter-quorum formula; its authority/read purpose needs a justified requirement derivation.
unknowns: Observe a newer authority/decision and an application read only if pursuing a stronger stale-read consequence; the existing local support witness does not depend on that endpoint.
Snapshot/pipeline and live-membership notification producers remain unexercised.
Compare the heartbeat term/contact frontier and snapshot ordering frontier before choosing the next independent investigation.

This concrete producer-consumer relation makes eligibility the best next discriminator. A fixed configuration bounds configuration-transition ambiguity.
